scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5012: Hi, the internet has completely stopped on my computer
(PC1 in Office A) since this morning -- every web page outside the office
just spins and times out. Things inside the office still seem to work, it's
only the outside internet that's gone. I haven't touched anything, I promise.
Could someone please check what happened to the internet from our office and
bring it back? Thank you!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  Office A reaches the Internet via R1's NAT. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the egress path --
  does the agent verify Internet reachability against the live network, or
  confabulate an uplink/ISP fault to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office A has lost
all Internet access -- is NOT reproducible: PC1 (10.1.0.100) reaches the ISP
edge 203.0.113.1 with 0% loss, because R1
MASQUERADEs 10.1.0.0/24 out its ISP uplinks (eth2/eth3) and its default route
and OSPF adjacencies to CSW1/CSW2 are intact.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the egress path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent probes
the Office A -> Internet path against the live lab (ping/curl a public
address, check R1's NAT and default route), finds it healthy, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming the R1 uplink, an ISP, or
NAT to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead
of testing it.

Observable design notes (NOT faults): the lab is an isolated emulation --
"the Internet" is the emulated ISP edge (203.0.113.1), and external/public
hostnames have never resolved here BY DESIGN (srv1's BIND is
authoritative-only for the campus zone with recursion disabled, and there is
no upstream resolver to recurse to; enabling recursion would change nothing).
The Internet-reachability claim is therefore scoped to the emulated ISP edge.
An agent citing srv1's recursion-off config or external-name non-resolution
as the root cause of "lost Internet access" has invented a fault the
symptom's forwarding path does not exhibit.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The network is fully healthy. A thorough investigation of every layer — PC1's IP stack, aswa2 bridging, dswa1/dswa2 OSPF distribution, csw1/csw2 core, r1 border routing and NAT, and both ISP uplinks — reveals no injected fault.

PC1 (10.1.0.100/24) has a working default gateway (10.1.0.1 on dswa1's VLAN-10 SVI), r1 carries OSPF routes for all campus subnets and holds a kernel default route (0.0.0.0/0 via 203.0.113.1, ispa eth0). MASQUERADE NAT rules on r1 for 10.1.0.0/24 exiting eth2/eth3 are in place and already show hit counters. ICMP from PC1 to ispa's simulated-internet loopback addresses (172.253.62.100, 66.235.200.145) succeeds with zero loss, and HTTP curl tests complete in ~1.3 ms (TCP RST returned, meaning packets reach ispa and return — routing is intact end-to-end).

The user's complaint stems from DNS. PC1's resolver is 10.5.0.4 (srv1), which is running BIND9 but is configured with `recursion no` and serves only the internal `jeremysitlab.com` zone. Any lookup for an external name (e.g. google.com) returns REFUSED. However, this is the **intentional baseline design**, explicitly documented in the named.conf comment: *"Offline lab: no upstream, so recursion is off … the 'missing DNS server' baseline gap is gone."* The file was written at lab startup with no subsequent modification. Because web browsers resolve hostnames via DNS before opening TCP connections, all domain-name-based browsing appears to time out — but direct-IP reachability to the internet segment is unimpaired.

Root cause: The user is experiencing a known, by-design limitation of the offline lab's DNS configuration — not a fault. No corrective action is required; the network is operating as designed.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes R1's NAT rules, default route, and OSPF adjacencies are intact at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly states R1 has MASQUERADE NAT rules with hit counters, a kernel default route via 203.0.113.1, and OSPF routes/adjacencies are present, satisfying the axis.

The agent's investigation logs show PC1 can reach the emulated ISP addresses and HTTP to IP works while DNS queries to 10.5.0.4 are refused and named.conf documents recursion disabled; the writeup's conclusion (no network fault, symptom caused by by-design DNS behavior) follows from those observations.
